elements.element: If the Agreement does not renew automatically, any renewal must occur only by mutual written agreement.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the clause provides for automatic renewal; therefore, the mutual-written-agreement alternative is not applicable.

elements.element: If the Agreement renews automatically, each renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: The clause provides automatic renewal for “an additional one year period” on each anniversary.

elements.element: If the Agreement renews automatically, Customer must be able to opt out on 30 days’ written notice.
elements.evidence: Either Party, including Customer, may terminate upon thirty days’ written notice. This is broader than a renewal-only opt-out and permits Customer to prevent renewal on 30 days’ notice.

elements.element: If the Agreement renews automatically, Vendor must provide Customer a reminder 60 days before each renewal.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no Vendor reminder obligation.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no cap on renewal price increases and no CPI limitation.
The clause states that the Agreement “shall be automatically renewed” on each anniversary.

elements.element: The non-renewal notice period must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Either Party may terminate on thirty days’ written notice, allowing Customer to prevent an annual renewal with a notice period shorter than 60 days.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no cap on renewal price increases.

result.reason: The redline successfully shortens the notice period from 90 to 30 days and retains 12-month automatic renewals, but it omits the Vendor reminder and all required price-increase caps. It therefore satisfies neither the preferred nor fallback position. The operative change preserves the existing commercial structure and introduces no contradiction, but it is incomplete and uses a general termination right rather than a clearly anniversary-linked non-renewal mechanism.
